title: Launch the design partner's three sites directly as shared-tier tenant deployments at M7 (never dedicated)
description:
Outcome: Ryan (2026-11-08, repeated): the design partner's three new sites launch DIRECTLY on the shared multi-tenant tier at M7, as tenant deployments created by data. They never start as dedicated sites; there is no dedicated launch, no later move and no migration runbook for them. Their launch is the M7 date, which is why the critical-path plan PPY-e38a2d exists. They are also the outside test of Prospectus cost accounting on the shared tier (PPY-25e0d7, kanbus-f45f7f).

Launch steps (each a data change, no code edit, no deploy): (1) an operator creates the partner's Account in Prospectus (if new) and three deployments of product papyrus through the Prospectus API (kanbus-271b4a); (2) Papyrus provisions each tenant from its deployment record (PPY-70a429) with the starter template (PPY-3aa10f); (3) the operator or the partner's admin sets each site's SiteConfig and BrandPack (name, logo, colours light and dark, allowed fonts, sections, nav, home template) through the site store (PPY-1252ce, PPY-c020ce, PPY-e572de) on the publication preset (PPY-cf7e6e); (4) the partner's admins sign in with Google on newsroom.p.apyr.us (PPY-fdbbd7, kanbus-3e5e82); (5) each site serves at <site>.p.apyr.us, and at its custom domain if the partner brings one (PPY-82de58, PPY-966722, kanbus-6daa8f). One site first, then the other two.

Readiness checklist (all true on production before the first partner deployment is created; these are M7's gates): (1) isolation enforced on the shared stack, adversarial suite green on the release (PPY-bdc4ee, PPY-f7ce77), security gate 1 signed off (PPY-3ff465) and, by default (decision D22), the external review done; (2) TI cut over and serving correctly from the shared stack (PPY-e51189); (3) data-only provisioning works on production (PPY-966ef5, PPY-70a429, PPY-e54eca); (4) both provisioning security reviews passed (PPY-1da916, Prospectus kanbus-fa72e8); (5) shared sign-in with the one shared Google client, token bound to the deployment (PPY-fdbbd7); (6) branding and layout as data (PPY-cf7e6e, PPY-1252ce, PPY-e572de, PPY-413576, PPY-3aa10f); (7) lifecycle and read-only rule wired (PPY-6cb44b, PPY-d7274f), export and deletion work (PPY-e882ee, PPY-62f10d); (8) cost accounting basics: shared stack tagged, model tokens and per-tenant shared usage reported to Prospectus, spend ceiling on (PPY-25e0d7, PPY-3fd951, PPY-49d059, PPY-889ab5); (9) runbooks rehearsed (PPY-7438d9).

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: features_backend/tenant-provisioning.feature and features_backend/cost-accounting-reports.feature, run for each partner site):
Scenario: A partner site goes live on the shared tier by a data change only
    Given every item of the readiness checklist is done on production
    When the operator creates the partner's deployment "<site>" of product papyrus in Prospectus
    Then the tenant is provisioned, its brand and sections are set as data, its admins sign in with Google on newsroom.p.apyr.us, and it serves at <site>.p.apyr.us with no code change or deploy

Scenario: A partner site's cost is attributed to its deployment
    Given a partner site that served pages and ran model work for a day on the shared stack
    When Prospectus imports and splits the day's shared cost
    Then the ledger shows that day's cost for app papyrus, the partner's Account and that deployment

Dependencies: blocked by the readiness tasks above (recorded as kbs dependencies). Blocks M7 (PPY-dad077), which closes when the three sites are live.

Testing: the scenarios on production per site; ledger compared with the per-tenant usage report for the first week.
Rollout: one site first, then two.
Risk and mitigation: Risk: schedule pressure to launch before isolation is proven. Mitigation: the checklist is the gate; time is saved on the critical path, never on the gate.

Releasable on its own: not applicable (launch).
DynamoDB index: none.
AppSync authorisation: unchanged.
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).
